args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying v2.3.1 to production, checkout-api failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service is healthy on v2.3.0 in all regions with an error rate of about 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failures, and find out why a release that was unhealthy in staging went to production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's passing health checks again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Before:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It was failing health checks with an error rate of about 18%.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to that version everywhere. After the rollback the service is healthy in all three regions, with an error rate of about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 says what happened and what I did. It lists two follow-ups:
  - Find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failures.
  - Find out why v2.3.1 reached production when its test version had already failed health checks in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
